title: Heavy, well constructed, knife handle is awkward and clumsy. Spoon shape is small
text:
Heavy, well constructed, knife handle is awkward and clumsy. Spoon shape is small. Forma is my fourth set of Mepra flatware so far. After listening to my husband rant about how much he dislikes our 20 year old silverware, I made a list of what he wants in good utensils. To that end, I have decided to try several of the Mepra designs until we find one we both love that we can afford and then I will buy a full 16 person collection. So....Forma isn't the one.

The utensils are well made and have a substantial feel to each piece when you hold them. These also have that beautiful intense shine that Mepra is known for. However, the spoons have a sort of tear drop shape to them that looks nice, but is actually inefficient for eating. The coffee/tea spoon is fine for those two things, but for eating ice cream it's a pain. It just feels wrong. The larger spoon is shaped wrong for twirling pasta into.

Finally, the knife. I dislike the design of this knife so much. The handle is angled differently than a traditional table knife. It does not lie flat on its side. Instead, it rests on the back of the handle with the serrated edge upright or the opposite direction, with the edge touching the plate or napkin surface. I get that this is a design or artistic thing, but it drives me nuts because in the real world after two meals, this knife is in the way - constantly.
